results.corrected_extracted: Four randomised trials, 284 participants: Avila 2024 (USA, 45 people: pouch, e-cigarette, no intervention); Caldwell 2010 (New Zealand, 63, cross-over of pouch, snus and nicotine gum, adverse events only); NCT04250727 (USA, 30: higher against lower strength, registry record only); Rensch 2023 (USA, 146, tobacco-industry funded: pouches of three strengths against a no-tobacco group and a continue-smoking group). All enrolled adults who smoked; three enrolled people not planning to quit; follow-up 7 days to 8 weeks. Ten ongoing studies are listed.
results.corrected_locator: Results › Description of studies › Results of the search; Included studies, Table 4 (overview), Study types, Participants, Interventions and comparators, Outcomes, Funding; Table 5 (per-study participant numbers)
results.note: Arms, 284 in total, funding, follow-up and ten ongoing studies match. The per-study numbers (45, 63, 30, 146) are in Table 5, added to the locator. The source says ongoing 'studies', not 'trials'; corrected.

results.corrected_extracted: Pouch against minimal control, abstinence at week 8: 1 of 18 given pouches had quit against 0 of 9 with no intervention; RR 1.58 (0.07 to 35.32), 1 trial, 27 participants (Avila 2024, high risk of bias); very low certainty (two levels for risk of bias and two for imprecision). The table's 11 per 1,000 and 18 per 1,000 are not the observed rates (0 of 9 and 1 of 18) and the review does not say how they were derived; the risk ratio and its interval match a 0.5 correction to each cell (editors' recalculation). Cigarettes per day among people still smoking at week 8: mean difference −1.07 (−12.72 to 10.58), 19 people with complete data.
results.note: Counts, RR, certainty, footnotes and cigarettes per day match. The review never says where the table's 11 and 18 per 1,000 come from; 'zero-event correction' was the editors' reading, though the RR and interval do match a 0.5 correction.

Counts, RR, 222 and 56 per 1,000 (7 to 449), 5 events, no risk-of-bias downgrade, cigarettes per day and carbon monoxide match. Editors' subtraction, 222 minus 56, gives 16.6 per 100, so 'about 17' holds.

All match: 2 of 15 against 0 of 15, RR 5.00 (0.26 to 96.13), log cigarettes per day MD -0.20, 13 of 15 with adverse events in each arm, two toxicity reports during dual use. Certainty not assessed, as stated.

All match Table 5: cough 5 against 3, breathlessness 6 against 1, similar by week 4; Rensch 86 events in 56 of 146, 76 mild, 10 moderate, 4 related, not split by arm; Caldwell side effects uncommon, fewer bad-taste reports.

results.corrected_extracted: Biomarkers against minimal control (Rensch 2023, tobacco-industry funded, high risk of bias, 53 people, about one week): NNAL mean difference −265.30 ng/g creatinine (−350.64 to −179.96) from a control mean of 330; COHb −6.7% (−8.33 to −5.07) from a control mean of 11.3%; 16 further biomarkers of exposure all favoured pouches with intervals excluding no difference. Very low certainty (risk of bias, imprecision). Against a no-tobacco group (46 people) none of 18 biomarkers clearly differed. Avila 2024 (19 people) found lower exhaled carbon monoxide with pouches than continued smoking, interval including no difference.
results.note: NNAL, COHb, control means, n = 53, 46 and 19, 18 biomarkers and 16 further ones all match. The page does not say all 16 further biomarkers are urinary, so 'urinary' is removed.

results.corrected_extracted: Rensch 2023 was funded by the pouch manufacturer (a tobacco company); the other three trials by philanthropic, academic or governmental bodies. The industry trial reported no smoking outcome, no serious events, and the largest set of biomarker results; the review states that its findings were consistent with the non-industry-funded studies. The review was funded by the US National Cancer Institute and the FDA Center for Tobacco Products through CAsToR 3.0; the review says no author took part in an included trial; no author declares funding from a tobacco, pouch or e-cigarette company (some declare payments from smoking-cessation medicine makers and public bodies).

results.note: Funding, 'no review author involved' and the declarations match. The cited Discussion paragraph also says the industry trial's findings were consistent with independent studies; added. Locator lacked the Methods statements (author involvement; CAsToR 3.0).

Matches: none at low risk; Avila, Caldwell and Rensch high, NCT04250727 unclear; performance bias high for Avila and Rensch (unblinded, different intensity), low for Caldwell. The 1st to 7th paragraph range holds.
